title: Red to Green
teaches: Red to green as we trade it: an entry trigger that rides on a setup that already qualifies, a leader pulling back to support above a rising 20-day EMA; the line is the prior day's close, the buy is a market order as price trades a cent over it after trading below it, no more than 4% above, the stop sits a few cents under the dip's low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R, and a loss at the stop is the plan working.

questions.q: Which price is the red-to-green line?
choices: The prior day's close
Today's opening price
Today's running VWAP
The prior day's high
questions.why: The prior day's official close. Red to green is a move from below the previous close to above it. The line is never the day's open or VWAP.
questions.lesson_line: The line is yesterday's close.

wrong.Today's opening price: A green candle is close over open. The red-to-green line is the prior close, never the open.
wrong.Today's running VWAP: VWAP is an intraday average. The line is the prior close, never VWAP.
wrong.The prior day's high: The high is a different level. The line is the prior close.

questions.q: A green candle, a close over the open, is a red to green while price is still under the prior close.
questions.why: False. Calling a green candle a red to green while the stock is still under the prior close is a named mistake. The line is the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: Over the open is not over the prior close.

questions.q: What is red to green on its own?
choices: An entry trigger on a setup
A standalone base pattern
A gap-up continuation setup
A reversal pattern at the lows
questions.answer: An entry trigger on a setup
questions.why: An entry trigger that rides on a setup that already qualifies. The setup is a leader pulling back to support. The cross of the prior close is the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Setup first. The cross is only the trigger.

wrong.A standalone base pattern: A base is a setup. Red to green is the entry for a stock that already qualifies.
wrong.A gap-up continuation setup: Red to green starts from a gap down or a red open, not a gap up.
wrong.A reversal pattern at the lows: The stock is a leader pulling back, not a stock at the lows.

questions.q: Every red-to-green cross on a gap-down day is a buy signal.
questions.why: False. Treating every red to green as a signal is a named mistake. Two of three gap-down days cross, and half fail by the close.
questions.lesson_line: The cross needs a setup under it.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: The pullback to support is the setup. The cross of the prior close is the ___.
questions.why: trigger. The pullback to support in a leader is the setup. The cross of the prior close is the trigger.
questions.lesson_line: Setup first, trigger second.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on a red-to-green buy?
choices: A few cents under the dip's low
At the prior day's close line
Under the 200-day average line
A fixed 8% under your fill
questions.answer: A few cents under the dip's low
questions.why: A few cents under the dip's low, which is the day's low at the time of the buy. Kullamagi: the stop is always the low of the day.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: under the dip's low.

wrong.At the prior day's close line: The prior close is the line you buy over, not the stop. A stop there sits just under your fill.
wrong.Under the 200-day average line: The 200-day is usually far below the dip. The stop is the dip's low.
wrong.A fixed 8% under your fill: A fixed percent ignores the dip. The stop sits under the low, within about 3%.

questions.q: Start with a small position and add to it as the cross holds.
questions.why: False. Full size at one price. No starter, no add. Starting small and adding on the cross is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: One price, full size.

questions.q: Which stock fits the setup under a red to green?
choices: RS 90, above 200-day, rising 20-day
RS 90, but under the 200-day line
RS 60, above 200-day, rising 20-day
RS 90, above 200-day, 20-day falling
questions.why: RS 90, above the 200-day with a rising 20-day EMA. A leader is RS 80 or more, above the 200-day, pulling back into support.
questions.lesson_line: Leader first. Then the pullback.

wrong.RS 60, above 200-day, rising 20-day: RS 60 is a laggard. A leader is RS 80 or more.
wrong.RS 90, above 200-day, 20-day falling: A falling 20-day EMA is a bounce in a correction, not a pullback in a trend.

questions.q: A leader that closes 15% over its 10-day average is a fine red-to-green setup.
questions.why: False. The prior close has to be within 10% of the 10-day average. Skip a long more than 10% above its 10-day average.
questions.lesson_line: Too stretched is too late.

questions.q: If the cross has not come by 10:30, there is no trade.
questions.why: False. There is no time-of-day rule. A quick cross is a grading factor, not a rule.
questions.lesson_line: A quick cross grades higher. A late one is not banned.

questions.q: In which market reading do red-to-green longs get full risk?
choices: Green
Yellow
Orange
Red
questions.why: Green. Full risk per grade comes with a Green reading. Yellow is smaller and fewer, Orange A+ only, Red mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: Green means full risk.

wrong.Red: Red is mostly cash and shorts.

questions.q: The day closes back under the prior close, so you sell at the close.
questions.why: False. A close back under the prior close the same day is a warning sign, not an exit. The stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: A warning is not an exit. The stop is.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: After trading below the prior close, price must trade at least one ___ above it.
questions.why: cent. After trading below the prior close, the stock has to trade at least one cent above it during regular hours.
questions.lesson_line: Under the line, then a cent over it.

questions.q: Prior close 329.07, open 325.97. How far below the prior close is the open, in percent?
questions.why: 0.94%. The prior close minus the open, divided by the prior close. The stock opened under the line, so it is red.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the gap from the prior close.

questions.q: Bought at 23.98, dip low 23.54, stop 3 cents under the dip low. How wide is the stop in percent?
questions.why: 1.96%. The entry minus the stop, divided by the entry. That is inside the 3% the stop usually keeps.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stop in percent before you size.

questions.q: Fill 111.93, stop 110.75. What price is 3R?
questions.why: 115.47. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of them to the fill. In our plan a third comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open.

questions.q: A stop-market order a cent over the prior close is the same as a market order on the cross.
questions.why: True. Entries are market orders. A stop-market order a cent over the prior close does the same job.
questions.lesson_line: Market order on the cross.

questions.q: Which of these helps a red to green?
choices: The index gapped down, got bought
The stock sits with no level nearby
The cross came late in the session
The 20-day EMA is falling fast
questions.answer: The index gapped down, got bought
questions.why: The index gapped down and got bought the same morning. That helps: the market is buying the same dip.
questions.lesson_line: The market buying the dip helps your cross.

wrong.The stock sits with no level nearby: Not at a level, in the middle of nowhere, weakens the case.
wrong.The cross came late in the session: A slow, grinding cross long after the open is the weaker cross.
wrong.The 20-day EMA is falling fast: A falling 20-day EMA is a bounce in a correction, not a pullback in a trend.

questions.q: Has it gone red to green?
choices: Yes, it crossed after trading under
No, it has not closed green as yet
No, it is still under today's open
questions.answer: Yes, it crossed after trading under
questions.why: Yes. It traded under the prior close, then at least a cent over it during regular hours. That is the red-to-green cross.
questions.lesson_line: Under the prior close, then a cent over it.

wrong.No, it has not closed green as yet: The cross is the first trade over the prior close, not the close of the day.
wrong.No, it is still under today's open: The open is not the line. The prior close is.

questions.story: The prior close was 50.00. The stock opened at 49.40, dipped to 49.30, then traded at 50.02 at 9:45.

questions.q: A stock that closed under its 200-day is a valid setup for a red to green long.
questions.why: False. The prior close has to be above the 200-day. No longs below the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day, or no long.

questions.q: A leader pulls back to a rising 20-day EMA, gaps down, then crosses the prior close. Which part is the trigger?
choices: The cross of the prior close
The pullback to the 20-day EMA
The gap down at the open
The rising 20-day EMA
questions.answer: The cross of the prior close
questions.why: The cross of the prior close. The pullback to a rising 20-day EMA in a leader is the setup. The cross is the entry.
questions.lesson_line: The cross is the trigger. The pullback is the setup.

wrong.The pullback to the 20-day EMA: That is part of the setup under the trigger.
wrong.The gap down at the open: The gap is how the stock gets red. It is not the trigger.
wrong.The rising 20-day EMA: That is part of the setup under the trigger.

questions.q: Setting the stop below the dip's low gives the trade room, so it is a good habit.
questions.why: False. A stop wider than the dip's low, set to give it room, is a named mistake. The stop only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: No extra room. The stop sits under the dip's low.

questions.q: Buy now, or wait?
choices: Wait for the trade through the line
Buy now; it is about to cross
Buy half now and half on the cross
questions.answer: Wait for the trade through the line
questions.why: Wait for the trade through the line. Buying under the line in anticipation is a named mistake. Bohen: wait for confirmation before entering a trade.
questions.lesson_line: No buying under the line.

wrong.Buy now; it is about to cross: Buying under the line in anticipation is a named mistake.
wrong.Buy half now and half on the cross: Full size at one price. No starter, no add.

questions.story: The stock is 20 cents under the prior close at 9:52 and looks like it will cross.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Hold; the stop is the exit
Sell at the close
Move the stop up under the close
questions.answer: Hold; the stop is the exit
questions.why: Hold. A close back under the prior close the same day is a warning sign, not an exit. The stop is the exit, and the stop at 94.67 is still below.
questions.lesson_line: A weak close is a warning, not a sell.

wrong.Sell at the close: A close back under the line is a warning sign, not an exit.
wrong.Move the stop up under the close: The stop only moves up toward breakeven at 2R to 5R. A close under the line does not move it.

questions.story: You bought the cross at 96.36 with the stop at 94.67. The day closes at 95.90, back under the line, above your stop.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Skip it; more than 4% over
Buy at market; it is running
Buy and give it a wider stop
questions.why: Skip it. Skip if the price is more than 4% above the prior close when you act. A stock already 4% green is a chase.
questions.lesson_line: Past 4% over the line is a chase.

wrong.Buy at market; it is running: 52.30 is more than 4% above 50.00. That is a chase.
wrong.Buy and give it a wider stop: The stop only moves up, never wider. And it would still be a chase.

questions.story: The prior close was 50.00. You look at 10:40 and the stock is at 52.30, green and running.

questions.q: Take the red-to-green long?
choices: No, Red is mostly cash and shorts
Yes, the setup is clean enough
Yes, but only at half size
questions.answer: No, Red is mostly cash and shorts
questions.why: No. In a Red market it is mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day. A leader's long waits for a better market.
questions.lesson_line: Red market: no long.

wrong.Yes, the setup is clean enough: A clean setup does not lift the market reading. Red is mostly cash and shorts.
wrong.Yes, but only at half size: Red is not a size rule. It is mostly cash and shorts.

questions.story: The market reading is Red. A leader above its 200-day gaps down onto its 20-day EMA and crosses the prior close.

questions.q: Is the report a problem?
choices: No, the report is already behind it
Yes, any earnings this month counts
Yes, only A+ setups after a report
questions.answer: No, the report is already behind it
questions.why: No. A red to green in a post-earnings flag is after the report, which is fine. The rule is no earnings in the next 3 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: After the report is fine. Before it is not.

wrong.Yes, any earnings this month counts: The window is the next 3 sessions. A report that is already out is fine.
wrong.Yes, only A+ setups after a report: No such rule. Only the 3 days before a report are off limits.

questions.story: A leader reported earnings last week and has flagged for four days on its 20-day EMA. It gaps down 1% and crosses the prior close.

questions.q: Which one is NOT a level the dip may tag?
choices: Today's VWAP
The 9-day EMA
The 50-day average
The 20-day EMA
questions.why: Today's VWAP. The dip tags the prior day's 9-day EMA, 20-day EMA, 50-day or 200-day, or a level we mark. VWAP is never the line.
questions.lesson_line: Tag a real level, not VWAP.

wrong.The 9-day EMA: That is a level the dip may tag.
wrong.The 50-day average: That is a level the dip may tag.
wrong.The 20-day EMA: That is a level the dip may tag.

questions.q: Higher volume on the reclaim is a plus, but there is no hard volume rule.
questions.why: True. There is no hard volume rule. Higher volume on the reclaim and a wider range are a plus, graded.
questions.lesson_line: Volume grades the cross. It does not gate it.

questions.q: Take the cross?
choices: Pass; it is a laggard
Take it; the cross is clean
Take it at half size
questions.why: Pass. A leader has an RS rating of 80 or more. This stock is a laggard.
questions.lesson_line: Buy leaders. The cross does not fix a laggard.

wrong.Take it; the cross is clean: The trigger needs a leader behind it. RS 55 is not one.
wrong.Take it at half size: Size does not fix a laggard.

questions.story: A stock with an RS rating of 55 gaps down 1% onto its 20-day EMA and crosses the prior close in the first hour.

questions.q: Bought at 96.36, stop at 94.67. The day closes at 95.90. How many R is the open loss?
questions.why: 0.27R. The close minus the fill, over your risk. The close is back under the line, but you are nowhere near the stop. It is a warning, not an exit.
questions.lesson_line: A weak close can still be a small loss in R.

questions.q: Account 100,000. You risk 0.75% and the position cap is 40%. Buy at 111.93, stop at 110.75. How many shares?
questions.why: 357 shares. The size is the smaller of the stop-based size and the cap. This tight stop would allow more, so 40% of the account divided by the price sets it.
questions.lesson_line: The size is the smaller of the risk size and the cap.

questions.q: What do you do at the open?
choices: Take the 3R trim at the open
Wait for 5R before you sell any
Add more at the open price
questions.answer: Take the 3R trim at the open
questions.why: Take the third at the open. A trim level the day opens past is taken at the open.
questions.lesson_line: Opens past a trim level, trim at the open.

wrong.Wait for 5R before you sell any: 3R is already past. If a stock opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
wrong.Add more at the open price: The full size goes in at one price. No adding.

questions.story: You bought at 111.93 with the stop at 110.75, so 3R is 115.47. The next morning the stock opens at 117.00.

questions.q: Take the fourth try?
choices: No, 3 tries a week is the limit
Yes, each cross is its own trade
Yes, but only at half size
questions.answer: No, 3 tries a week is the limit
questions.why: No. At most 3 tries a week and 6 a month on one stock, and after the third failed attempt we stop trying.
questions.lesson_line: Three failed tries and the week is done.

wrong.Yes, each cross is its own trade: Each cross is a new trade, but the cap is 3 tries in a week.
wrong.Yes, but only at half size: Half size does not lift the cap.

questions.story: A stock crossed the prior close three times this week and each time fell back to your stop. A fourth cross prints on Friday.

questions.q: Has it gone red to green?
choices: No, a green candle is not the line
Yes, the hourly candle is green
Yes, price rose a lot from the low
questions.answer: No, a green candle is not the line
questions.why: No. A green candle is a close over the open. The line is the prior close, and price is still under it.
questions.lesson_line: Over the open is not over the prior close.

wrong.Yes, the hourly candle is green: A green candle is a close over the open. The line is the prior close.
wrong.Yes, price rose a lot from the low: Rising from the low is not crossing the line. 79.10 is still under 80.00.

questions.story: The prior close was 80.00. The 10:30 hourly candle opened at 78.60 and closed at 79.10, a green candle. Price is 79.10.

questions.q: A slow, grinding cross long after the open is a B-minus cue.
questions.why: True. A quick cross inside the first hour that does not chop grades higher. A slow, grinding cross long after the open is a B-minus cue.
questions.lesson_line: Quick and clean grades higher.

questions.q: A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold.
questions.why: True. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Dead money gets freed.

questions.q: A stop 1% to 2.5% under the entry is an A+ cue, and a stop over 3% is a B-minus cue.
questions.why: True. A stop 1% to 2.5% under the entry grades higher. A stop over 3% is B-minus, and the size comes from the stop.
questions.lesson_line: A tight honest stop grades higher.

questions.q: Is light volume a no-trade?
choices: No, volume is a cue, not a gate
Yes, 0.6x is too light to trust
Yes, add only on the next day
questions.answer: No, volume is a cue, not a gate
questions.why: No. There is no hard volume rule. Higher volume is a plus, graded. This cross ran 3R in 2 days on light volume.
questions.lesson_line: Volume grades the cross. It does not gate it.

wrong.Yes, 0.6x is too light to trust: There is no hard volume rule. Light volume was ANF's one blemish and it still ran.
wrong.Yes, add only on the next day: No adding. The full size goes in at one price.

questions.story: A leader flagged on its 20-day EMA, gapped down and crossed the prior close in the first hour. Volume is 0.6x of average.

questions.q: Take it at full size?
choices: No, size down by the stop or skip
Yes, the setup is clean
Yes, with the stop pulled in to 3%
questions.answer: No, size down by the stop or skip
questions.why: No. The stop sits within about 3% of the entry. A dip too deep for that means skip or size down by the stop. Never tighten it.
questions.lesson_line: Size from the honest stop.

wrong.Yes, the setup is clean: A clean setup does not shrink the honest stop.
wrong.Yes, with the stop pulled in to 3%: Never tighten a stop to fit. The dip's low is where the setup is wrong.

questions.story: A leader gaps down onto its 20-day EMA and crosses. The honest stop under the dip's low is 3.44% under the buy.

questions.q: A green close. Was the stop wrong?
choices: No, a green close is not a free pass
Yes, you should have sold at the close
Yes, the stop should have been wider
questions.answer: No, a green close is not a free pass
questions.why: No. A green close is not a free pass: the stop was still 1.2% under the buy and one red open took it. The stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: A green close does not move the stop.

wrong.Yes, you should have sold at the close: A green close is a good sign, not an exit. The stop is the exit.
wrong.Yes, the stop should have been wider: Never a stop wider than the dip's low. The stop only moves up.

questions.story: You bought at 181.60 with the stop at 179.43. The day closed green. The next morning the stock opened red and took the stop.

questions.q: What grade?
choices: B-minus; the 20-day EMA is falling
A+; the cross came in hour one
No trade; the gap is too small
questions.why: B-minus at best. A flat or falling 20-day EMA is a B-minus cue. The setup is a pullback in a trend, not a bounce in a correction.
questions.lesson_line: Rising 20-day, or the grade drops.

wrong.A+; the cross came in hour one: A quick cross helps, but a falling 20-day EMA is a B-minus cue.
wrong.No trade; the gap is too small: The card does not rest on a gap size here. The falling 20-day EMA is what costs the grade.

questions.story: A stock above its 200-day gaps down 1% and crosses in the first hour. But its 20-day EMA is falling and it sits 13% under its 50-day.

questions.q: What helped this red to green?
choices: The market gapped, then got bought
The stock was a weak metals laggard
The cross came late, after lunch
questions.answer: The market gapped, then got bought
questions.why: The market gapped down and was bought the same morning. That helps. The leader had flagged four days on its 9-day EMA.
questions.lesson_line: A dip the whole market buys is stronger.

wrong.The stock was a weak metals laggard: CDE was a metals leader. A laggard weakens the case.
wrong.The cross came late, after lunch: It crossed in hour one, which is the quicker cross.

questions.q: Red to green or Oops?
choices: An Oops reversal first
A plain red to green
A Kicker
questions.why: An Oops reversal first. An Oops opens below the prior day's low and reclaims that low. A red to green only needs a dip under the prior close.
questions.lesson_line: Under the low and back is an Oops.

wrong.A plain red to green: A day that undercut the prior low and reclaimed it is an Oops first.
wrong.A Kicker: A Kicker opens above the prior close. This opened below the low.

questions.story: The stock opened under yesterday's low and reclaimed that low by 10:15.

questions.q: Red to green or Go Signal?
choices: A red-to-green, not a Go Signal
A Go Signal off the 2 pm cross
An Oops reversal at the open bar
questions.answer: A red-to-green, not a Go Signal
questions.why: A red-to-green trigger. A cross at 2 pm, or with no flag under it, is a trigger, not a Go Signal. A Go Signal is the red to green with a timer and a level.
questions.lesson_line: No flag, no timer: only a trigger.

wrong.A Go Signal off the 2 pm cross: A Go Signal needs a timer and a flag under the cross. A 2 pm cross with no flag is neither.
wrong.An Oops reversal at the open bar: An Oops opens under the prior low. Nothing here says that.

questions.story: The cross came at 14:00. There was no tight hourly flag under it.

questions.q: Can a Kicker be a red-to-green entry?
choices: No, it never starts under the line
Yes, it is the cleanest of them all
Yes, if it gaps up on huge volume
questions.answer: No, it never starts under the line
questions.why: No. A Kicker opens above the prior close and never trades back to it, so it cannot go red to green.
questions.lesson_line: Red to green needs a red start.

wrong.Yes, it is the cleanest of them all: A Kicker is never red at the open, so it cannot cross the line from below.
wrong.Yes, if it gaps up on huge volume: Volume changes nothing. A Kicker still opens above the prior close and never starts under the line.

questions.story: A Kicker gaps up and trades through the prior day's high at the open. Someone calls it the cleanest red to green.

questions.q: Red to green, or another setup?
choices: Another setup; it is a news gap
A red to green; it crossed the line
A Kicker; it gapped
questions.answer: Another setup; it is a news gap
questions.why: Another setup. Buying a big news gap down because it ticked green is a named mistake. QuantRocket: stocks keep dropping after large down gaps.
questions.lesson_line: A big news gap is not a red to green.

wrong.A red to green; it crossed the line: A big news gap is a gap setup, not this trigger. A small gap leaves the uptrend intact.
wrong.A Kicker; it gapped: A Kicker gaps up. This gapped down.

questions.story: A leader gaps down hard on a fraud probe and a guidance cut. It ticks green at 10:40.

questions.q: Short it?
choices: No, no shorts above the 200-day
Yes, it is the mirror of red to green
Yes, if the stop is tight
questions.why: No. Never short a green to red in a leader above the 200-day. In the Go Signal that move is the shakeout before the long. Shorts are only below the 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: Green to red in a leader is a shakeout.

wrong.Yes, it is the mirror of red to green: The mirror only applies below the 200-day. A leader above it is a shakeout.
wrong.Yes, if the stop is tight: A tight stop does not change the rule. No shorts above the 200-day.

questions.story: A leader above its 200-day opens green and falls through the prior close in the first hour.

questions.q: Take the cross?
choices: Pass; nothing is under the dip
Take it; the cross was in hour one
Take it with a wider stop
questions.answer: Pass; nothing is under the dip
questions.why: Pass. The dip low sat 2.9% above the nearest level, and the rule is within 1%. It was a trigger with no setup under it.
questions.lesson_line: A cross with no level under it is only a trigger.

wrong.Take it; the cross was in hour one: A quick cross helps the grade. It cannot replace a level under the dip.
wrong.Take it with a wider stop: The stop only moves up, never wider. And there is still no setup.

questions.story: A leader gaps down 1.4% and crosses in the first hour. The dip low is 188.24. The nearest level, the prior day's low, is 182.94.

questions.q: Take the cross?
choices: Pass; a report is 3 sessions away
Take it; the setup is clean
Take it and sell before the report
questions.answer: Pass; a report is 3 sessions away
questions.why: Pass. A report was due inside the next 3 sessions. Three sessions before earnings, B22 says no new buy.
questions.lesson_line: Clean cross, near report: no buy.

wrong.Take it; the setup is clean: A clean setup does not lift the earnings window.
wrong.Take it and sell before the report: A plan to sell later does not lift the rule. No new buys in the 3 days before a report.

questions.story: A leader gaps down onto its 50-day and crosses in the first hour. Its report is due 3 sessions from now.

questions.q: Which cross grades higher?
choices: The 9:50 cross on a gap that holds
The 13:30 cross after chopping
They grade the same
questions.answer: The 9:50 cross on a gap that holds
questions.why: The 9:50 cross that holds. A quick cross inside the first hour that does not chop back and forth is the stronger case. A slow cross after chopping is weaker.
questions.lesson_line: Quick and clean beats slow and choppy.

wrong.The 13:30 cross after chopping: A slow, grinding cross long after the open is the weaker cross.
wrong.They grade the same: The clean first-hour cross grades higher.

questions.story: Cross A came at 9:50 on a 0.9% gap that held. Cross B came at 13:30 after the stock chopped across the line four times.

questions.q: Which red to green grades higher?
choices: A, the stronger case
B, it has more room to run
They grade the same
questions.why: A. It is a true leader above a rising 20-day, the market is buying the dip too, and the cross is quick. B has RS 74, under 80, so it is not a leader.
questions.lesson_line: Leader, rising average, level and market all line up.

wrong.B, it has more room to run: B is not a leader. RS 74 is under 80.
wrong.They grade the same: A is a leader and B is not.

questions.story: Setup A: RS 94, above a rising 20-day, 50-day and 200-day, the index gapped down and got bought, a quick cross. Setup B: RS 74, a flat 20-day, not at a level, a late cross.

questions.q: The stop fills at 12:30. Was the trade a mistake?
choices: No, a planned loss at the stop
Yes, the stop was too tight
Yes, wait for the close next time
questions.answer: No, a planned loss at the stop
questions.why: No. The second hour closed back under the line and the stop went at 12:30. The first-hour cross is the fast one and the whippy one. The loss was the plan.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out under the rules is a planned loss.

wrong.Yes, the stop was too tight: The stop sat under the dip's low, where the rule puts it. A wider stop only makes the loss bigger.
wrong.Yes, wait for the close next time: Waiting for the close is not the trigger. The cross is.

questions.story: You bought the first-hour cross at 194.80 with the stop at 190.33. The second hour closes back under the line and the stop fills at 12:30. The day closes red.

questions.q: What did the close back under the line tell you?
choices: A warning; the stop was the exit
A signal to buy more
A reason to move the stop lower
questions.answer: A warning; the stop was the exit
questions.why: A warning. The stock spent the whole day under the line and the stop went in the last hour. A close back under the prior close is a warning sign, and the stop is the exit.
questions.lesson_line: The warning came. The stop was the exit.

wrong.A signal to buy more: No adding. The full size goes in at one price.
wrong.A reason to move the stop lower: The stop only moves up, never down or wider.

questions.story: You bought at 424.08 with the stop at 416.07. The stock spent the day under the line, closed at the bottom of its range, and the stop filled at 15:30.

questions.q: Take the retry?
choices: Yes, a new trade with its own stop
No, the first stop-out ends the name
Yes, with the old stop
questions.answer: Yes, a new trade with its own stop
questions.why: Yes. After a stop-out, buy again only if the setup triggers again, as a new trade with its own stop. The retry on 2026-09-15 at the same level ran 14.8R.
questions.lesson_line: A retry is a new trade, inside the cap.

wrong.No, the first stop-out ends the name: The cap is 3 tries a week and 6 a month. One stop-out two weeks ago does not end it.
wrong.Yes, with the old stop: A re-entry is a new trade with its own stop and every rule.

questions.story: A leader was stopped out the same day at its 20-day EMA two weeks ago. Today it gaps down onto the same level and crosses again. You have had no tries this week.

questions.q: Take the cross?
choices: Pass; the 20-day EMA is falling
Take it; it crossed the line
Take it with a smaller stop
questions.why: Pass. The 20-day EMA is under its value 5 sessions earlier. That is a bounce in a correction, not a pullback in a trend.
questions.lesson_line: Rising 20-day, or no pullback in a trend.

wrong.Take it; it crossed the line: The cross needs a setup under it. A falling 20-day is a bounce in a correction.
wrong.Take it with a smaller stop: Never tighten a stop to fit. And the setup is missing.

questions.story: A stock gaps down and crosses the prior close in the first hour. Its 20-day EMA is under its value 5 sessions ago, and the stock is rolling over.

questions.q: Take it?
choices: Take it: market order on the cross
Wait for the close, then buy
Pass; it opened red
questions.answer: Take it: market order on the cross
questions.why: Take it. A leader at a rising 20-day EMA, a gap down that tags it, the cross of the prior close, a Green market and no report near. Market order on the cross, stop a few cents under the dip's low.
questions.lesson_line: Setup, trigger, stop: buy the cross at market.

wrong.Wait for the close, then buy: The trigger is the first trade over the prior close. Waiting for the close buys later at a worse price.
wrong.Pass; it opened red: Opening red is how a red to green starts. Red to green needs a dip under the line.

questions.story: A leader drifts two weeks to its rising 20-day EMA. It opens at 325.97 against a prior close of 329.07, dips to 323.88, then trades over 329.07 in hour one. The market is Green and the report is weeks away.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the day before a gap down. The daily chart shows the pullback and averages, not RS or the hourly cross. Watch or pass?
choices: Watch for the cross; 20-day is rising
Pass; the 20-day EMA is falling
Pass; it is under the 200-day
questions.answer: Watch for the cross; 20-day is rising
questions.why: Watch for the cross. A two-week drift down to a rising 20-day EMA in a leader is the setup. The next day it gapped down onto the line and crossed in hour one.
questions.lesson_line: A pullback to a rising 20-day is the setup.

wrong.Pass; the 20-day EMA is falling: Look again: the 20-day EMA is rising under the pullback.
wrong.Pass; it is under the 200-day: Price sits above the 200-day, resting on its 20-day EMA.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the day before a gap down. The daily chart shows the 20-day EMA, not RS or the hourly cross. Watch or pass?
choices: Pass; the 20-day EMA is falling
Watch for the cross; it is a leader
Watch; it is above the 200-day
questions.why: Pass. The 20-day EMA is under its value 5 sessions earlier. A cross in a stock rolling over is a bounce in a correction, not a pullback in a trend.
questions.lesson_line: No rising 20-day, no setup under the cross.

wrong.Watch for the cross; it is a leader: Strength in the past is not the test. The 20-day EMA has to be rising now.
wrong.Watch; it is above the 200-day: Above the 200-day is one line. A falling 20-day EMA fails the other.

questions.q: Where does the stop go?
choices: Just under the dip's low
Just under yesterday's low at 92.10
Under the 50-day average
questions.why: Just under the dip's low. A stop wider than the dip's low, set to give it room, is a named mistake. The stop only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: Under the dip's low. No extra room.

wrong.Just under yesterday's low at 92.10: That is wider than the dip's low, set to give it room. It is a named mistake.
wrong.Under the 50-day average: The stop is the dip's low, not a far average.

questions.story: You buy the cross. The dip low is 94.70. Yesterday's low was 92.10 and you would like more room.

questions.q: QuantRocket found that stocks tend to recover after small down gaps and keep dropping after large ones.
questions.why: True. QuantRocket: stocks tend to recover after small down gaps and keep dropping after large down gaps. A small gap leaves the uptrend intact.
questions.lesson_line: Small gaps get bought. Big news gaps keep falling.

questions.q: An orderly pullback, flag, inside day or higher low in the last few sessions is the structure we want before the cross.
questions.why: True. Structure before the cross: an orderly pullback, flag, inside day or higher low. It is graded rather than measured from one bar.
questions.lesson_line: A calm pullback first, then the cross.

questions.q: What becomes the stop?
choices: The first 30-minute low
The old stop at 38.50
The prior close
questions.why: The first 30-minute low. A gap against the stop is decided by the first 30 minutes, and here the loss stays under 2R. Past 2R, get out.
questions.lesson_line: On a gap against the stop, the first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.The old stop at 38.50: The gap went through it. The first 30 minutes decide the new stop.
wrong.The prior close: The prior close is the line you bought over. After a gap against the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop.

questions.story: You hold a red-to-green winner overnight. You bought at 40.00 with the stop at 38.50. The next morning it gaps down to 38.04. The first 30-minute low is 37.50.

questions.q: Does it pass our floor?
questions.story: A leader pulls back to its 20-day EMA, gaps down and crosses the prior close. It trades at 8.40 a share and averages $30 million a day.
choices: No; price must be at least $10
Yes, $30 million a day is plenty
No; it needs $50 million a day
Yes, leaders skip the price floor
questions.answer: No; price must be at least $10
questions.why: No. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. This one fails on price.
questions.lesson_line: Two checks: $10 a share and $20 million a day. Fail either and skip it.

wrong.Yes, $30 million a day is plenty: The dollar volume passes, but the price does not. Both checks must pass.
wrong.No; it needs $50 million a day: The floor is $20 million a day, not $50 million. It fails on price.
wrong.Yes, leaders skip the price floor: Leaders get no exception. Price must be $10 or more.

questions.q: The stock trades 1,500,000 shares a day on average at 12.00. How many dollars a day is that?
questions.why: $18 million a day. Shares times price. That is under the $20 million floor, so the stock fails even though it is over $10.
questions.lesson_line: Shares times price is dollars a day. Check it against $20 million.

questions.q: How many shares do you buy?
questions.story: Your risk math says 40,000 shares. The stock trades 3,000,000 shares a day on average. The setup is clean and the stop is tight.
choices: 30,000, the 1% ceiling
40,000, the risk math
45,000, the clean setup
60,000, double for the tight stop
questions.why: 30,000. We never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume. The ceiling caps the risk-based size.
questions.lesson_line: Check the volume ceiling after the risk math. It caps the size.

wrong.40,000, the risk math: That is over 1% of 3,000,000 shares. The ceiling caps the size.
wrong.45,000, the clean setup: A clean setup does not lift the ceiling. It is 1% of the daily volume.
wrong.60,000, double for the tight stop: A tight stop does not lift the ceiling. It is 1% of the daily volume.

questions.q: Holding 8,000 shares of a stock that averages 1,000,000 a day is under our volume ceiling.
questions.why: True. 8,000 shares is under 1% of the average daily volume, which is our ceiling.
questions.lesson_line: Compare your share count to the daily volume. One percent is the ceiling.

questions.q: A stock averages 2,400,000 shares a day. What is the most shares you may own, at 1% of that?
questions.why: 24,000 shares. One percent of 2,400,000. Owning more is over our ceiling.
questions.lesson_line: Move the decimal two places: 1% of the daily volume.

questions.q: Where does the stop on the rest go?
questions.story: You bought the red to green at 96.36 with the stop at 94.67. The stock hits 3R and you sell a third.
choices: Up to your fill price, breakeven
Stay put under the dip's day low
Up to the 3R price where you sold
Just under the 10-day average line
questions.answer: Up to your fill price, breakeven
questions.why: Up to your fill price. The stop goes to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.
questions.lesson_line: First trim at 3R, stop to breakeven. The rest runs risk-free.

wrong.Stay put under the dip's day low: At the first trim the stop moves up to breakeven by default.
wrong.Up to the 3R price where you sold: That locks in a profit target as a stop. Breakeven is the fill price.
wrong.Just under the 10-day average line: The 10-day is the trail for the last third, not the breakeven move.

questions.q: Move the stop to breakeven the moment the day turns green after your buy.
questions.why: False. The stop moves to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default. A green day is not 2R.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven waits for 2R at least. Do not tighten it on the first green tick.

questions.q: Fill 111.93, stop 110.75. Where is 5R?
questions.why: 117.83. One R is the fill minus the stop. Five of those added to the fill is where the second third comes off.
questions.lesson_line: Write your 5R price down. The second third comes off there.

questions.q: Next step at 5R?
questions.story: You sold a third at 3R and moved the stop to breakeven. The winner now trades at 5R, and two thirds are still open.
choices: Sell a third more, trail the last
Sell all the rest and bank the 5R
Hold the rest; raise the stop to 3R
Add a third more at the new high
questions.answer: Sell a third more, trail the last
questions.why: Sell another third and trail the last. After the first third at 3R, another third goes at 5R.
questions.lesson_line: Thirds at 3R and 5R, then trail what is left.

wrong.Sell all the rest and bank the 5R: The last third is trailed, not sold at 5R.
wrong.Hold the rest; raise the stop to 3R: The second third comes off at 5R. Raising the stop does not replace it.
wrong.Add a third more at the new high: The full size is bought at one price. No adding.

questions.q: Complete the trail rule.
questions.sentence: A fast mover's last third is sold on a close under the ___-day average.
questions.why: 10. Fast movers trail the 10-day. Steadier ones trail the 21-day. Sell on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: Fast mover, 10-day. Steadier name, 21-day.

questions.q: Do you sell the last third?
questions.story: You hold the last third of a red-to-green winner. It is a steady name that has ridden its 21-day for weeks. Today it closes under the 10-day but above the 21-day.
choices: No, hold; the 21-day is its trail
Yes, a close under the 10-day exits
Yes, sell half of the last third
No, hold; trail the 50-day instead
questions.answer: No, hold; the 21-day is its trail
questions.why: No. A steadier name trails the 21-day, and it is still above it. Sell on a close below that line.
questions.lesson_line: Pick the trail that fits the stock. Sell on a close under it.

wrong.Yes, a close under the 10-day exits: The 10-day trails fast movers. This steady name trails the 21-day.
wrong.Yes, sell half of the last third: The rule is a sale on a close under the trail average, not a half step.
wrong.No, hold; trail the 50-day instead: The defaults are the 10-day and the 21-day, not the 50-day.

questions.q: A steadier name trails the 21-day average, while a fast mover trails the 10-day.
questions.why: True. The last third trails the 10-day for fast movers and the 21-day for steadier ones.
questions.lesson_line: Match the trail to the mover: 10-day fast, 21-day steady.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You bought a red to green ten trading days ago and it closed green that day. Since then it has drifted and sits at 0.5R. The stop has not traded.
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 days
Hold; the green close proved it
Hold; the stop has not traded yet
Add a little to lower the average
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold. The green close on day one does not change that.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days under 1R and the trade is done. The money moves on.

wrong.Hold; the green close proved it: The green close was on day one. After 10 trading days under 1R, the time stop sells it.
wrong.Hold; the stop has not traded yet: The time stop is its own exit. Under 1R after 10 days, it is sold before the stop trades.
wrong.Add a little to lower the average: No adding: full size at one price. The time stop sells a trade that has not worked.
